## TL;DR

Close-outs now validate up to `maxParallelValidations` queued jobs at once (default 2, range 1–8). Publishing to `main` stays serial in queue order, and a job whose base moved is re-validated before it can publish. This session I merged main into the branch, checked each finding from review pass 1 against the current code, and re-ran the scoped gate. The gate did not pass cleanly on the first runs: it failed with timeouts and one session-persistence assertion that all pass when run alone, and it finished green only once the machine was idle. I have not reproduced the thinkpad-only failure. Visual shots are declared but not yet verified against a captured preview.

## Work and rationale

Scheduling is a pure function, `selectCloseOutStarts` in `src/server/integration-job.ts`, so the server pump and the tests share one definition. It walks the pending queue in enqueue order, skips jobs that already run, and stops at the limit. A job in `publishing` starts only when it holds the publish turn, so the head of the queue is the only job that can merge. A job that finishes validating early parks with its candidate intact.

The pump in `src/server/server.ts` (`pumpCloseOutJobs`) runs on enqueue, after each run's `finally`, and on a 30-second timer while a pressure hold strands work. The pressure guard holds only extra concurrency. The first run always starts, as the single-job pipeline did, and `holdExtra` stops every later start in the same pass.

Per-run state lives on a fresh `CloseOutOrchestrator` created by `newCloseOutOrchestrator(taskId)`, so two runs never share an attempt or a stamped-done set.

For a moved base I kept the existing guard rather than adding a cheaper re-merge. `publishCandidate` still compares `baseMainSha` with `main` under the repo and root locks. Bookkeeping-only drift publishes directly. Real code drift returns the job to `syncing`, which rebuilds and re-gates the candidate, bounded by `MAX_PUBLISH_DRIFT_RETRIES`. The brief allowed a cheaper re-merge only if it was provably safe. I could not prove that without running the gate, so it fails closed.

The config key `maxParallelValidations` is wired through `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, `loadConfig` (with the string fallback the other numeric keys use), `getConfigSchema()` as a select in Settings → General → Close-out (`settings-location.ts`), `SUPPORTED_TOML_KEYS`, and `user-docs/configuration.md`. `docs/close-out-pipeline.md` describes the scheduler, the publish turn and the stale-base rule.

Review pass 1 flagged five classes. I checked each against the current tree rather than the tree it was written against:

- **Pressure guard bypass.** `pumpCloseOutJobs` consults the guard whenever work is waiting, and `selectCloseOutStarts` holds every start after the first. This is no longer a bypass.
- **Cancellation lifecycle.** `selectCloseOutStarts` starts cancelled jobs before the publish-turn and limit checks, so a parked cancelled publisher is torn down without waiting behind a stalled head.
- **Pipeline UI contract.** Parallel jobs sit in `snap.parallel`, not `queue`. The drawer close-out row, the card watch list, `IntegrationStatusBar`, `integrationPipelineRole`, `integrationRunningEntry` and `integrationQueuePosition` all read that list. Queue position counts from `queueDetail`, which numbers every live job.
- **Merge conflict.** Merging main into the branch produced no conflicts. The task file already matched main, so I took nothing from the branch.
- **Visual verification.** Still open. The declared shots are in the task body. I have not confirmed they render the parallel row or the Settings control against a captured preview.

## Approaches tried

I considered a cheaper re-merge for a moved base and rejected it for the reason above. I also considered keeping `queuePosition` as validation order. I kept it as publish order, because overlapping `validating` jobs have no meaningful queue order and callers rely on position 0 being the next job to publish.

I checked the cancellation path by reading the code, not by running a live cancel against an overlapping run. The overlap tests exercise `selectCloseOutStarts` directly, not the live pump.

## Challenges and blockers

The first scoped `repoos check --changed main` run got through build and format, then stopped at the remote-validation step with no exit line. The process was gone, so it was not a result. I reran with `--local-tests`. That run exited 1 with four failures in two files:

- `tests/handoff.test.ts`: two tests timed out at 15 s, and one asserted a formatting failure in a fixture worktree.
- `tests/session-persistence.test.ts`: one assertion that a session persisted before boot read `undefined`.

I ruled out the formatter. `bun run fmt:check` passes on all 1,822 files. Both suites pass when run alone (48 and 50 tests). Those failures look like load-sensitive timing under a parallel run, which the repo's flake guidance describes, rather than a regression in code this branch touched. I could not show that from the failure text alone, so I re-ran the gate on an idle machine. The final result is recorded in the handoff status, not claimed here.

The thinkpad failure in the queued message (`gate exit 1 on thinkpad`) does not reproduce locally. I have no access to the thinkpad log from this worktree, so I cannot say which test it hit.

Overlapping `git` writes to the candidate object store and ref namespace have not been load-tested. The docs say so. A ref-lock collision would surface as that job's sync failing, not as a stale publish. A human should run a multi-host close-out burst before relying on it at scale. I cannot prove that from this worktree.

## Key learnings

Keeping the scheduler rules in one pure function made the overlap, ordering and held-start cases testable without a live server. Keeping the stale-base guard exactly where it was meant the new code never had to decide whether a candidate was current. It only had to decide which job reaches that guard.

Once jobs overlap, phase and queue position have to be read together. A `validating` job can sit at any position, and a `publishing` job that is not at position 0 is parked. The pipeline doc is the one place that says so.

Reviews written against an earlier tree can list defects already fixed. Re-checking each finding against the current code before editing saved effort and kept the diff honest.
